Amazon's Black Friday sale is in full swing, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers. Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save big on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

Recent findings suggest that the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the tech giant introduced a upcoming model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

If you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

If you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

Sources indicate that if you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

If you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is presently $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

In a recent development, the newly introduced Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

If you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's right now pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

It has been revealed that if you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, currently marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

Industry observers note that if you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (currently $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

For about $30 more than the X4 Classic, you can upgrade to the Xteink X4 Pro, which happens to be Lifehacker's e-reader Gift of the Year pick. It offers all the perks of the other Xteink devices, with two critical quality-of-life upgrades: A touchscreen for easier navigation, and a temperature-adjustable front light so you can read it in a dark room. (Less obviously, it also has a slightly faster processor that makes the whole thing feel a little snappier.) Right now, the X4 Pro is at its lowest price ever when ordered directly from Xteink: $84, or around 15% off the usual $99 price.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

It has been revealed that the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is the best Kindle deal most people should buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. This is a good option if you don't care about maxing out storage or getting rid of lock screen ads.

Sources indicate that if you read a lot of material that uses color, like comics or some colored manga, the extra money for a color e-reader is definitely worth it. Check out the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft for a good option.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the funniest scenes in Taika Waititi's 2014 vampire mockumentary, What We Do in the Shadows, happens when the central group of vamps bump into a rival werewolf gang on a late-night stroll. "Look out guys, don't catch fleas," one of the vampires remarks, leading to an escalating exchange of insults, snarking, and howling, but no actual violence. (In this world, neither vampires nor werewolves are particularly brave, despite their extraordinary powers.).

According to recent reports, at the time, the interaction, while hilarious, also made perfect sense. Popular culture was deep in the thrall of Stephenie Meyer’s Twilight, which famously pits a vampire and a werewolf against each other for the affections of a human girl. But a decade later, the idea that vampires and werewolves would be natural enemies seems a bit odd.

In a recent development, having grown up in the early 2000s, I’ve always seen vampires and werewolves as mortal enemies. Yet, as someone fascinated with them both (though I’ll admit that, as a dog lover, I’m a little more partial to werewolves than vampires), I’ve always wondered: where did the supernatural beef between two of horror's most iconic creatures even come from? The answer reveals that while this rivalry isn't as old as you might think, it's also an inevitable outcome based on the origins of these two classic monsters.

When you turn to classic literature for answers about the feud between vampires and werewolves, you first have to look back at their origins. To be frank, this is impossible: ancient mythology and cultures around the world are vast and varied. Pinpointing a single location, person, or story as their origin is ludicrous. Instead, we have to explore a selection of stories — and boy, is there plenty to choose from.

Recent findings suggest that ancient mythology is full of stories in which humans are transformed into wolves as punishment. In the Epic of Gilgamesh, Gilgamesh refuses to mate with the goddess Ishtar because she had previously turned a shepherd into a wolf. And in Greek mythology, Zeus transforms King Lycaon into a wolf after the cheeky king attempts to trick the god into eating Lycaon’s son, Nyctimus.

In a recent development, meanwhile, John William Polidori’s 1819 novel The Vampyre portrays vampires as specters of desire, corruption, and manipulation, with Lord Ruthven in The Vampyre and Bram Stoker’s Dracula using their powers to kill and seduce in equal measure. In both cases, these creatures are clearly associated with the very concept of evil.

Recent findings suggest that similarly, both undergo a transformation. The vampire, once human, dies and is reborn, with a craving for blood and, depending on the source, otherworldly abilities​​​​​​​ such as transformation (Dracula literally turns into a wolf in Stoker’s novel) and flight. The werewolf, however, is still very much alive but loses its humanity when it transforms and is reduced to lupine instincts​​​​​​​.

It has been revealed that given their many similarities, how did vampires and werewolves come to be seen as natural enemies by the 2000s? There are two very different explanations.

Industry observers note that the first comes from the world of tabletop games, specifically publisher White Wolf's The World of Darkness series, which includes 1991's Vampire: The Masquerade and 1992's Werewolf: The Apocalypse. Although Vampire: The Masquerade mainly focuses on politics among vampire clans, the conflict between vampires and werewolves also plays a significant role. The hostility, however, seems unequal:​​​​​​​ werewolves hate vampires far more than vampires hate werewolves. Vampires are too busy obsessing over one another to pay any attention to their lupine enemies.

However, vampire and werewolf fans often point to another answer when discussing the feud: the action-horror fantasy movie series Underworld, created by Kevin Grevioux, Len Wiseman, and Danny McBride. The films mostly follow Selene (Kate Beckinsale), a vampire death dealer caught up in the centuries-long war between the two factions. With stilted acting and an overreliance on skin-tight leather outfits, the Underworld franchise has aged pretty terribly, but no one can deny that the 2003 film was the perfect vehicle for popularizing the rivalry White Wolf had already established. Indeed, White Wolf even tried to sue Sony Pictures over it.​​​​​​​.

With Underworld’s popularity at the time (the first film grossed about $95.7 million worldwide), it seemed that more and more media began portraying the two creatures’ hatred as an ancient blood feud. The origin of this rivalry often differs by IP​​​​​​​, but it still largely comes back to the creatures being foils for each other​​​​​​​, right down to how they present themselves.

In a recent development, vampires are often portrayed as aristocratic, in control, and free-thinking. They may have an insatiable desire for blood, but they can blend into everyday society well enough, with their monstrosity often hidden in the shadows. On the other hand, werewolves are depicted as savages, unable to control themselves and fueled by a rage and hunger driven by the Moon.

According to recent reports, in Underworld, vampires live in a mansion, throw fancy parties, and follow a structure that resembles nobility. Werewolves, by contrast, live in the sewers. Though they also have a leader, the pack structure means its members are generally considered equals.

It has been revealed that there’s also something to be remarked for the sheer hype of watching two otherworldly creatures battle. As someone who’s turned my nose up at people getting worked up over Godzilla movies (it’s just two massive creatures fighting! What’s the big deal?), I have to sheepishly admit that vampires versus werewolves can get me just as worked up.​​​​​​​.

Sometimes, you just want fantasy creatures ripping each other limb from limb, and it’s even better when it’s two creatures portrayed as hating one another for years.

Decades have passed since the early 2000s, and while many of those years were defined by the clash between these two supernatural creatures, recent years have shown less interest in exploring that same scrap.

Sources indicate that that’s not to say people have lost interest in the topic. AMC’s adaptation of Interview with the Vampire remains beloved by viewers, while director and writer Robert Eggers’ Nosferatu enchanted plenty of horror fans in 2024. This year, Eggers hopes to do the same for werewolf fans with Werwulf. Interest in the fantastical worlds of vampires and werewolves has not faded​​​​​​​, not by a long shot. (And maybe if we're lucky, Eggers' next movie will pit his two monsters against each other.).

Whether the vampire-versus-werewolf beef will ever be renewed to the extent it was in the early 2000s, however, remains to be seen. Netflix is developing an animated series adaptation of Midnight Sun, which is Twilight from Edward Cullen's perspective, and Underworld creator Len Wiseman recently gave a positive update on production of an Underworld TV series. If any IPs can rekindle the vampires-versus-werewolves wars​​​​​​​, they’re these two​​​​​​​. (Sadly, the What We Do in the Shadows werewolf spinoff, We're Wolves, has been stuck in development hell for years.).

Whether we need or want that to be the case, however, is another matter entirely. For the moment, the quarrel between the two creatures is largely in the past. Could Hollywood move forward and instead see the two monstrous factions pair up? Weirder things have happened.

Industry observers note that I've recently started listening to the audiobook of Killing Floor, the first of Lee Child's Jack Reacher novels, and having watched the first season of Reacher a few times now, it's quite difficult not to picture Alan Ritchson sitting in that diner in Margrave when you're listening to the opening chapter. From the police station to the barbershop where Reacher learns a little more about Blind Blake, Prime Video did a particularly good job of bringing Child's fictional Georgia town to life. I mentioned this to Child when we spoke recently for the release of the latest Reacher novel, Chain Reaction, and having assumed that the production team had found a suitably picturesque little town somewhere in Canada in which to shoot the series, I was quite surprised by his response.

The production team behind the first season of Reacher actually built Margrave from scratch in a field in Ontario, with Child explaining that the restrictions imposed during the COVID-19 pandemic had made shooting in existing locations particularly difficult. “That was a unique production, that Season 1, because it was COVID, and it was not possible to film in existing locations. They built that town," Child told Collider.

In a recent development, when I asked Child if they'd actually built the entire town for the purposes of shooting eight episodes of television, he explained that they had, and that the set had subsequently found another use. “They built Margrave on a huge open field about an hour from Toronto," Child explained. "They literally built every square inch of it, and happily they managed to sell it to the Ontario Film Board afterwards, so that you can just lay down the signs and make it look a bit different for future productions.”.

According to recent reports, given that Reacher spends much of his time traveling around the United States, it's quite impressive how much of America the production team has managed to find in Canada. Child explained that there's considerably more to the appeal of shooting in Ontario than the financial incentives initially responsible for bringing productions there. He told Collider:.

“It's a virtuous circle, and it started a long time ago with tax breaks up there, and therefore it snowballed. So there's great facilities, great studios, great union crews up there. The more you go there, the better it gets. And so it really is a big center.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

John Hughes made some of the most beloved movies of all time in his eight directorial efforts, to the point where it's nearly impossible to rank the films he wrote and directed. Still, there are few movies that reach the specific balance of comedy with such an emotional punch as Hughes does in 1987's "Planes, Trains and Automobiles." This is a goofball movie that borders on the surreal, with some of the most bizarre imagery in a comedy movie, while also delivering some of the most heartbreaking and heartwarming moments that came out of the 1980s.

The film stars Steve Martin as Neal Page, an uptight marketing executive forced to be paired with Del Griffith (John Candy), a goofball salesman with a heart of gold, when their journey from Newly introduced York City to Chicago is disrupted. What was meant to be just a short cab and plane ride home just in time for Thanksgiving ends up being a three-day odyssey full of shenanigans, attempted murder, and much more.

It's no wonder, then, that "Planes, Trains and Automobiles" is the No. 1 movie streaming on Paramount+ on Thanksgiving Day 2026. After all, there are plenty of movies about Christmas, to the point where it's easy to overlook Thanksgiving, and with good reason. For one, it's not really a holiday outside the U.S. and Canada (and even then, celebrated on different days), and the imagery is not dissimilar to Christmas anyway. Still, the best Thanksgiving movies deliver a very specific tone that's less about holiday magic and more about celebrating what we have despite the horrors of daily life. From the opening minutes of "Planes, Trains and Automobiles," it's clear this movie could not be set at any other time of year except during the chaos and anxiety of Thanksgiving.

Sources indicate that the travel chaos that is quite unique to Thanksgiving is the crux of "Planes, Trains and Automobiles." The arrival of snowstorms that plague the East Coast of the continental United States, the huge flux of travelers, and the general anxiety and irritability of travelers around the country add to, well, a very stressful time of year. It's why Steve Martin's uptight businessman Neal is so relatable. The film simply nails the feeling of needing to interact with others and ask for their help while being utterly frustrated with having to deal with anyone at such a bad time. It's also why John Candy's performance is such a tightrope, because his character has to be annoying in addition to being charming. Del's not really someone you'd want as a travel companion, yet he is absolutely the best person you want as a friend.

According to recent reports, that tricky balance is what makes the movie so memorable, and why John Candy's best line remains the best Thanksgiving movie quote ever. Neal and Del are forced to not only set aside their differences, but actually recognize the humanity in each other while acknowledging that they themselves are flawed. This is a highly empathetic film that's all about how we should find love and camaraderie even in unlikely companions. That is why the film so perfectly captures the spirit of Thanksgiving, because it's not about estranged family members, but rather complete strangers who must come to learn they need one another and that they should be grateful for what they bring into each other's lives. Togetherness is not just for family members, or even people you like, but also for strangers you come to appreciate despite the ways they annoy you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Netflix's four-season science fiction TV series is great from start to finish, and even its weakest episode is miles better than the sci-fi reveals you'll find on other streamers. Netflix's sci-fi offerings are not quite at the level of a streaming app like Apple TV, with its huge library of great shows in the genre, but it still has some winners.

Netflix has taken shots at a variety of genres and storytelling styles, sometimes hitting it out of the park but missing badly on other occasions. It has managed to carve out one niche, though, and that's with anthologies. Black Mirror, Guillermo del Toro's Cabinet of Curiosities, and Beef are all celebrated anthologies.

One of its best is also one of the streamer's best science fiction shows, Love, Death & Robots. The four-season, 45-episode anthology series consists of 6–21 minute shorts, all animated and written by different creative teams, with a handful of groups double-dipping over the seasons.

Industry observers note that the only thing uniting the stories, save for the occasional multi-parter, is that they each deal with one of the themes of the title, and often deal with more than one. Love, Death & Robots premiered in 2019, and has had such illustrious directors as David Fincher craft their own episodes.

Recent findings suggest that with 45 episodes, you would think that more than a handful wouldn't make the grade, but Love, Death & Robots is one of the rare shows where every episode is worth watching. There are certainly some that are worse than others, but even the least of them stands up to the best other sci-fi shows can offer.

The worst episode of Love, Death & Robots is probably not objective, considering how unique each episode is, and how varying animation styles, tones, and subject matter will appeal to everyone differently. However, a good case can be made for "Life Hutch" being the worst. Then again, another case can be made for it still being very watchable.

Season 2, episode 7, is "Life Hutch", an episode that uses photorealistic animation and stars Michael B. Jordan as Terence, a space pilot who gets stranded on a desolate planet and fights a murderous robot. Jordan could certainly have been used better, and the flashbacks take up too much time that a short episode simply doesn't have to spare.

It has been revealed that however, there's still a lot going for it, including the animation that will have you wondering if everything is actually live-action with a few CGI touch-ups here and there. Jordan may be underused, but even a little Jordan is better than no Jordan. "Hutch" probably ranks low on most people's "best of" Love, Death & Robots lists, but that doesn't mean they're skipping it.

Love, Death & Robots makes every episode of the series watchable by giving each creative team total freedom to tell their story. If someone wants to make a classic sci-fi tale of mech-suits fighting alien invaders, they are free to. If they want to put on a Red Hot Chili Peppers concert with characters designed like marionettes, they can do that too.

There's a lot of freedom on display in Love, Death & Robots, and even the episodes that don't work as well still showcase creators putting exactly what they want on screen. You don't sense an invisible hand guiding the Love, Death & Robots episodes; it's a show for animators and writers as much as it is for the audience.

You can switch noise modes and, on an iPhone, activate features like Personalized Spatial Audio in Settings. They last up to 32 hours with ANC on, which is longer than both the more expensive Sony WH-1000XM6 and AirPods Max 2.

According to Beats, the 360 offer up to 1.75 times the noise cancellation of the Beats Studio Pro. PCMag’s review, which gave the headphones an “Excellent” rating, was impressed by how well they blocked out everything from plane engine noise to café chatter. The noise cancellation falls short of pricier models, and PCMag found the Sony WH-1000XM4C slightly better in that respect.

The PCMag review claims the headphones deliver “nice, deep bass, reasonably crisp highs, and a more neutral tuning than you might expect for a pair of Beats headphones.” If you’re after long battery life, rich audio, and plush earcups you can swap for a pop of color, $249 is a great price for the Beats 360 headphones.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alarms are one of the most notable iPhone features, and iOS 27 offers a key feature that should help your alarm actually wake you: a upcoming volume setting for alarms that’s independent of other volume settings.

Industry observers note that have you ever accidentally slept through an alarm? We’ve all done it. And most often for me, it’s because my alarm volume was unintentionally set to a very low level.

According to recent reports, I suspect that’s a pretty common reason for missed alarms. And in iOS 27, Apple finally has the fix—but it requires manually setting up.

Inside Settings ⇾ Sounds & Haptics, you can now set a volume for alarms that’s independent from the systemwide ringtone setting.

iOS 27 has two fresh sections in this Settings screen: Alarms and Timers, and Alerts and System Sounds. Both include ‘Match Ringtone Volume’ toggles that are on by default. This means your volume for alarms, timers, alerts, and other system sounds are all determined by the ringtone volume.

But if you disable the Alarms and Timers toggle, you’ll get a upcoming volume slider that applies only to those system functions, and won’t be impacted by your ringtone volume.

As seen above, this means you can crank the Alarms and Timers volume up to the maximum level without making every other system sound, including notifications and phone calls, be similarly deafening.

So the next time you sleep through your alarm, it won’t be because the alarm was too quiet.

In case you missed it, iOS 26 introduced a welcome feature that lets you set custom snooze durations for alarms, and also an option to have alarms trigger on your iPhone even if you’re wearing an Apple Watch.

Do you plan to set a custom volume setting for alarms in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments.

There are classic Christmas movies like "It's a Wonderful Life" and "National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation," and then there are the Christmas movies that we just watch every year because they're on repeatedly, forcing their way into the holiday zeitgeist, regardless of quality. "Jingle All the Way" is one of those movies.

It's a cinematic masterpiece compared to "Jingle All the Way 2" with Larry the Cable Guy, proving it's a Christmas movie that didn't need a sequel.

But one of the best parts of "Jingle All the Way" comes from the interaction that Schwarzenegger's Howard Langston has with his deceptively thoughtful, sleazy neighbor Ted (the late, great star of "Saturday Night Live" and "The Simpsons," the one and only Phil Hartman). That's where we get one of the best Christmas movie quotes of all time.

The 2017 German sci-fi mystery thriller series Dark aired for three seasons on Netflix, gaining critical acclaim and a global cult following. Its complex plot explored the paradoxical nature of time travel through strange mysteries in the fictional town of Winden, Germany.

Sources indicate that six years after its finale, series creators Baran bo Odar and Jantje Friese are producing a new mystery thriller, Sonnental. HBO Max Germany released a 30-second teaser for the series, introducing the plot and the protagonist played by Dark star Lisa Vicari.

In a recent development, sonnental shares Dark's spooky atmosphere and eerie woodland setting, but the new series is a crime mystery rather than sci-fi. The plot follows a series of murders based on Der Struwwelpeter, a German book that features 10 stories about misbehaving children whose actions have terrible consequences. In the teaser, we hear the voice of a child singing the first verse of "The Story of Wicked Frederick," the second story in Der Struwwelpeter.

"Der Friederich, der Friederich,.

This translates to "Frederick, Frederick, he was a terrible tyrant." The tale is about a boy who abuses and tortures animals. When a dog Frederick whips bites him, the child becomes ill and bedridden and the dog eats all his food. HBO says the book's twisted tales will become "deadly nightmares" in Sonnental, so Frederick's karmic punishment may be even more sinister. All six episodes of Sonnental will premiere on HBO Max in March 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This Thanksgiving, after the turkey and stuffing, Angel Studios is dishing up dessert with their sweet biopic Hershey, about the rise of one of the world’s largest chocolate manufacturers in the world. In this interview with Collider’s Steve Weintraub, stars Finn Wittrock and Alexandra Daddario discuss the real couple behind this American dream.

Sources indicate that directed by Mark Waters, Hershey follows the story of Milton Hershey (Wittrock) and his wife Kitty (Daddario), as they defy the odds, from bankruptcy to success. But when Kitty falls ill, she inspires Milton to reach for an even bolder dream: to build a legacy that would continue to give to others for years to come. Wittrock and Daddario are joined by David Costabile as Tobias Thornhill, Richard Kind as Joseph Royer, and Alan Ruck as Henry Hershey.

In this interview, Wittrock and Daddario discuss the energy on set, take after take of chocolate, and what they learned about the Hersheys through their research. They also play a game of “Keep or Cut,” and Daddario shares her thoughts on the hit Disney+ series Percy Jackson.

COLLIDER: Alex, are you watching Percy Jackson or are you like, “No chance?”.

In a recent development, ALEXANDRA DADDARIO: No, I would absolutely watch it, but I don't watch TV because my excuse is always my child, but it's true. I barely can find time to watch TV lately. But I love the fact that there's a show, and we were just at the Empire State Building.

FINN WITTROCK: It was cool. The Empire State Building was all decked out.

According to recent reports, DADDARIO: The whole thing. It's just so cool. It's been almost 20 years since I did that first movie, and it's just so cool to see that it's still so popular. It's great.

You guys have worked on a lot of intense shoots, and I'm just curious, where does the intensity of making Hershey rank when there are a lot of takes where you're eating so much chocolate and candy, shooting a movie?

WITTROCK: The takes do add up. The first three of eating chocolate are really fun, and then you get to take 15, and….

DADDARIO: You can't have lunch some days because you know that you're going to be eating so much chocolate.

Industry observers note that WITTROCK: It's a good problem to have. It's not the worst problem that there could be.

DADDARIO: I know! We’re complaining about eating too much chocolate.

Marvel is bringing back Wolverine's biggest bad, but as an ally. It is as true in superhero comics as it is in professional wrestling: when a bitter blood feud has reached an epic, 5-star payoff, sometimes there is nowhere else for the two combatants to go as enemies, so instead the best creative choice is to pair them up as a tag team. That is exactly what is set to happen in January, as part of Marvel's "Feral Wolverine" arc.

In a recent development, warning! Spoilers ahead for Marvel's "Feral Wolverine" arc!

That storyline kicks off next week, with Wolverine #30, and Marvel is promising a bloodbath. The problem is that it will be "innocent blood that stains [Wolverine's] hands and claws" this time, if he can't "rein in his bestial temperament," as the synopsis for the concern puts it. The synopsis for the following issue mentions a trail of "blood and death," but it also teases "the help of an unexpected ally." The thing is, Marvel has already spoiled who it is going to be. A villain who has been dead since 2024.

According to recent reports, and not just any villain. Wolverine's archnemesis, Sabretooth. Following his dramatic death at Logan's claws at the end of the spectacular "Sabretooth War" arc, Victor Creed is finally back in the mix in the main Marvel timeline. The "how" is TBD, but the "why" seems clear, as surprising as it might be: to help Wolverine when he's at his lowest point.

Recent findings suggest that the art for one of Wolverine #31's variant covers gives away Sabretooth's return, but artist Ian Churchill renders them in familiar form. That is, at each other's throats. Crashing out of what appears to be a hotel window, plummeting toward the swimming pool below. Cover art, especially variant cover art, doesn't always correspond to what is going to happen in the issue, but this image seems so specific that it might, in this case.

Sources indicate that either way, with Wolverine in a state of "feral fury" in the issue, even helping him is going to involve fighting him. If nothing else, Sabretooth will give Logan a target to focus on that can fight back, keeping him from going on a rampage and hurting civilians, more than he already might have.

Beyond that, though, Marvel has already tipped its hand narratively, in terms of how this latest round in the renewed rivalry between Sabretooh and Wolverine will play out. The synopsis and cover for Wolverine #32 spoil the swerve in their historic feud, which will have them fighting side-by-side again for the first time in years.

"Logan reunites with...Victor Creed?!" That's how the synopsis for Wolverine #32 puts it. The cover shows the two running into battle together. There is good reason to be flummoxed by this. The last time the two met in the present-day Marvel Universe, it was after Sabretooth waged a campaign of terror against Wolverine, attempting to destroy everything and everyone Logan loved before killing him permanently. Sabretooth very nearly succeeded, but in the end, he was the one who was dispatched by Wolverine.

It was a fitting send-off for the villain, but this is Marvel Comics. Sabretooth's death was never going to last forever, or for very long. He has made subsequent appearances in flashbacks, and as an apparition, and in alternate continuities, but now he's confirmed to be resurrected in the mainstream Marvel canon.

Recent findings suggest that sabretooth has had tenures, throughout his X-Men history, as an anti-hero. Even a borderline hero at times. This might or might not be the start of that. Considering the fact that it will be hard for Sabretooth to top his "Sabretooth War" actions as a villain, a redemption arc might be the best option for the character right now. Marvel fans will find out over the course of 2027, as the year kicks off with the villain's return as the "unexpected ally" who might just save Wolverine from himself.

MagSafe Monday: Anker’s MagGo Pro 2 has a built-in fan to keep 25W Qi2.2 charging from slowing down

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The biggest glitch with Qi 2.2 on MagSafe batteries is the slowdown caused by heat.
  • MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.
  • Heat is the enemy of MagSafe charging, which is why it slows to a crawl on a hot day and why most MagSafe batteries can’t hold their top speed for an entire charge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest glitch with Qi 2.2 on MagSafe batteries is the slowdown caused by heat. It doesn’t matter if the battery specs say it can charge at Qi2.2 speeds if the heat slows it down after 15 minutes. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro directly targets heat with a built-in fan in the MagSafe battery.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

Heat is the enemy of MagSafe charging, which is why it slows to a crawl on a hot day and why most MagSafe batteries can’t hold their top speed for an entire charge. Anker’s answer in the MagGo 2 Pro is a small fan inside of it. Anker says it keeps the charging surface below 96.8°F, and the fan adjusts its speed based on what’s plugged in and how the charge is progressing. You can switch between Cool and Silent modes if you don’t want to hear it running at all.

The result of having this fan is a Qi2.2 power bank that actually reaches Qi2.2 speeds for a full charge. Anker rates it at 25% on an iPhone 17 Pro in 10 minutes, then to 50% in 25 minutes, which is the kind of speed you’d normally expect from a wired charging session.

In a recent development, the MagGo 2 Pro battery is 10,000mAh, which is enough for a little over one full charge of an iPhone Pro Max and closer to two on a standard iPhone. Size-wise, it has about the same footprint as the iPhone itself and is roughly an ounce lighter than Anker’s standard MagGo. It’s not a slim battery, but for one with a fan, it’s workable in your travel bag, crossbody, etc.

The single USB-C port works both directions at up to 45 watts. If you plug in a 45-watt charger to it, the MagGo 2 Pro can charge from empty to 80% in under an hour. The same port will charge a Mac or an iPad up to 45 watts in a pinch, which is a nice add-on for a MagSafe battery. You are not going to charge up your MacBook Pro from zero to full with it, but it’s a nice way to get a little charge in an emergency at the airport, etc.

One thing to know before you buy: the cable in the box is a 1-foot USB-C-to-USB-C cable, and Anker says that reaching the full 45-watt recharge speed requires a 45-watt-rated cable. So keep that in mind as you pack for a trip.

Anker put a small display on the side that cycles through six screens with a side button: charging wattage, battery percentage, battery health, and temperature. It’s a nice touch to know you are reaching the 25-watt Qi 2.2 speed.

Recent findings suggest that there’s also a built-in stand that adjusts from flat to 80 degrees and folds back into the body when you’re done. You can also quickly turn off charging if you simply want to use it as a stand. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro comes in Phantom Gray, Burgundy Red, Polar Night Blue, and Starlight Silver.

Qi2.2 is the Holy Grail of MagSafe chargers, but as I noted in the beginning, it’s irrelevant if the heat throttles it. To get full 25-watt MagSafe charging on the go, you’ll likely need something with a fan, unless you’re in colder weather. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro solves that problem with a built-in fan, a handy side display, and a stand.

The Anker MagGo 2 Pro is available on Amazon and directly from Anker.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This article contains, you guessed it, spoilers for "Blade Runner 2099.".
  • After two movies, several short films, the anime show "Black Lotus," and numerous novels and comics, how many directions are left to take the "Blade Runner" franchise?
  • It has been revealed that those who've read Philip K.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More spoilery than spoilers. This article contains, you guessed it, spoilers for "Blade Runner 2099.".

After two movies, several short films, the anime show "Black Lotus," and numerous novels and comics, how many directions are left to take the "Blade Runner" franchise? Well, that's easy. You simply go back to the original source material. "Blade Runner 2099" creator and showrunner Silka Luisa embraced the tall task of picking up the classic story where previous media left off — by going straight to the book that inspired it all.

It has been revealed that those who've read Philip K. Dick's "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?" will recognize the author's fingerprints all over the Mercerism plotline that rises to the fore late in "Blade Runner 2099." In the novel, this idiosyncratic religion centers on Wilber Mercer, a holy figure who climbs a mountain on a pilgrimage. The catch is, he does so while having rocks thrown at him mercilessly, inspiring the idea to recreate his torturous ascent through a virtual reality device known as an empathy box. This was one of the biggest aspects that both "Blade Runner" movies completely skipped, preferring to focus on the more grounded details of this cyberpunk world while eschewing the spiritual.

In a recent development, that finally changes here, as I discussed with Luisa during a press junket. "I was always fascinated by Mercerism," she explained. "Just the idea that there was a religion that was technology-based where people would be completely isolated, but then join through technology so that they could feel empathy with each other — that feels so current." She went on to theorize:.

According to recent reports, "If you sold [empathy boxes] today, I genuinely think people would buy them. There is this deep longing for connection, and we no longer know how to get in a room and be with each other.".

Given the digital horrors we've normalized on an everyday basis in recent years (the impending threat of a superintelligence bent on our destruction, generative AI, and the ever-present hellscape that is social media), it's not too much of a leap to take "Blade Runner 2099" creator Silka Luisa at her word about Mercerism. Somewhere, there almost certainly would be a segment of the population all too happy to strap themselves into an empathy box device and electroshock themselves into feeling the same pain that Wilber Mercer supposedly did. (Of course, his entire ascent is eventually revealed to be a staged incident that never actually happened, but that's neither here nor there.).

But, even more than that unsettling hypothetical, Luisa had an even better reason to introduce the concept of Mercerism into "2099." As she excitedly told me:.

Sources indicate that "[...] Just from a creative and an imagination standpoint, it was so exciting to be like, 'Okay, I only have a couple words of description here, but what does an empathy box look like? How do we find references from the real-world that we can build out into it?'".

In the series, Michelle Yeoh's Replicant Olwen gets an up close and personal experience with an unfriendly Mercerite cultist. For Luisa, this provided a unique opportunity to flesh out what was in the scripts:.

Recent findings suggest that "Trying to design the murals that are in the chapel, all the little paraphernalia that would go with it, who would be practitioners of it. That's just such fun world-building that, I mean, what other show are you gonna get to do that on?".

All eight episodes of "Blade Runner 2099" (you can read our review here) are now streaming on Prime Video.

  • Recent findings suggest that the movie focuses on a gifted cellist named Alex Serian (Pascal), who returns home to Los Angeles after 20 years on the road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pedro Pascal is one of the biggest, most in-demand actors in Hollywood right now. "The Mandalorian" star is as massive as he's ever been, especially since he's part of the full cast of "Avengers: Doomsday," which arrives in December. He's reprising his role as Reed Richards from last year's "The Fantastic Four: First Steps." And yes, that's going to be a must-see cinematic event for people all over the world, but Pascal is starring in another movie that demands to be seen in theaters as well.

It has been revealed that "Behemoth!" is not as substantial as "Doomsday." In fact, I'd go so far as to wager a lot of people reading this are probably hearing about it for the first time. It's a smaller drama that might not typically earn the "must-see in theaters" label in the streaming era. Be that as it may, it's absolutely worth prioritizing in theaters, as watching it at home is going to leave a whole lot to be desired in comparison.

Recent findings suggest that the movie focuses on a gifted cellist named Alex Serian (Pascal), who returns home to Los Angeles after 20 years on the road. Music completely consumes him, but a turn of events leads him on an unexpected journey that completely alters his life. That's the gist of it, without spoiling some of the more compelling details that are better discovered while watching the movie.

Tony Gilroy is the man who made "Andor" within the "Star Wars" galaxy, but he's also a very talented filmmaker outside of that franchise (see "Michael Clayton"). This represents his return to the director's chair for a feature film for the first time in 14 years. It's a very welcome one at that. It's also arguably Pascal's greatest performance to date in his impressive career. But none of those very good reasons to see this movie are why it demands to be seen in a theater.

It has been revealed that "Behomoth!" is a non-linear character study through the lens of a man's singular obsession with music and how that complicates his important relationships outside of that obsession. It's a f*****g good movie. But it's also very much a movie about music and the love of music, so it should come as no surprise that it also contains some incredible music. That's why this movie is so greatly enhanced by the theatrical experience.

It has been revealed that I was lucky enough to catch this one at the Austin Film Festival this year, and from the opening scene, the swell of the orchestral arrangements hit me like a brick wall. With all due respect to the theater I was in, it's not like I was in a fancy IMAX auditorium or a decked out Dolby Cinema screen. It was just a damn good theater. But that made all of the difference.

Even as someone who cherishes the theatrical experience and considers himself a blockbuster junkie (as evidenced by my favorite movies of all time), this isn't the type of movie that I'd normally scream about needing to be seen in a theater. However, Tony Gilroy and the movie's wildly impressive list of composers, which includes everyone from Michael Giacchino to Alan Silvestri, outdid themselves. The sound hits you like a train, and no matter how good most people's home audio setup is, it's just not going to compare.

In a recent development, "Trolls World Tour" was the least likely movie that changed Hollywood forever, making it possible to watch upcoming releases at home. That coupled with the rise of streaming has made it easier than ever for people to stay home and watch movies. When they do go to theaters, it's not for "little" dramas like this. But this movie is absolutely a spectacle in its own way, making it worth seeking out.

I'm not trying to lower one movie to raise the other. I'm going to see "Avengers: Doomsday" on opening night. I'm very excited about it. The "Avengers: Doomsday" ticket pre-sales have already topped the entire run of "Supergirl." That movie doesn't need anyone's help. Nobody needs to be told to get off the couch for that one.

Industry observers note that "Behemoth!" is a movie that doesn't scream "must-see spectacle" on the surface. But the craft on display is enthralling, and the sound is nothing shy of a minor miracle of cinema. It's a love letter to music and a cautionary tale about obsession, with both sides of that coin benefitting marvelously from the experience that only a movie theater can offer. Watching movies at home has never been better, but it's still not quite the same thing.

Also, let me again remind you that Tony Gilroy made the modern masterpiece that is "Michael Clayton." That's absolutely the filmmaker who is back in the saddle for this one, alongside Pedro Pascal giving it all in a role that he was made for. The stars aligned for this one, and it's absolutely, rightfully going to be in the awards season conversation. But it's also at risk of being one of those movies that gets lost in the flow at the box office as bigger things surround it.

I'm here to tell you this: "Behemoth!" is not a "wait to stream it" movie. No matter how it may look on the surface, this is precisely the kind of cinematic experience people claim to crave. Something original and worthy of leaving the house for. This is worth the time and money, even if it's not a $100 million blockbuster. It's spectacular in its own way.

"Behemoth!" hits theaters on December 4, 2026.

Sources indicate that the holiday shopping season is here, and Apple Watch is always a popular gift. Apple’s lineup includes the affordable Apple Watch SE 3 and the more advanced Apple Watch Series 12.

Here’s how those two Apple Watch models stack up….

In a recent development, the Apple Watch SE 3 is the most affordable way to enter the Apple Watch ecosystem. It got a massive update last year, adding a variety of new higher-end Apple Watch features. It now offers an Always-On display, sleep apnea notifications, temperature sensing, interactive wrist flick and double tap gestures, and more.

The Apple Watch SE 3 offers 18 hours of battery life, though you can stretch that to 32 hours in Low Power Mode. It supports fast charging, going from 0-80% in 45 minutes.

Even though it hasn’t been updated in a year, the Apple Watch SE 3 is a very compelling option, especially for people fresh to the Apple Watch ecosystem. It’s pretty fantastic that you can get an Apple Watch with key display and health-monitoring features for under $200.

It has been revealed that the Apple Watch Series 12 is Apple’s newest smartwatch, and it’s a big update over its predecessor. This year, Apple doubled down on the health and fitness capabilities of Apple Watch with an all-new Health Sensing System.

Apple touts that the Apple Watch Series 12 delivers “the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable.” In fact, the company conducted a study of more than 1,000 participants that found the Series 12 “achieved statistically better overall accuracy than every competing wearable it tested across workouts and daily activities.”.

With the new system, Apple Watch Series 12 captures your heart rate every five seconds. Previous Apple Watch models, including the Apple Watch SE 3, take measurements every five minutes. The new Health Sensing System also enables a new readiness score feature, which factors in your recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score.

As I wrote in my review, the Apple Watch Series 12 brings some of the biggest improvements to Apple Watch health tracking in years. The new sensing system unlocks a trove of new data along with better accuracy.

Sources indicate that the Apple Watch lineup is incredibly strong right now. Whether you’re deciding between the SE 3 and Series 12, both offer great health tracking, battery life, and connectivity. The Apple Watch SE 3 is an excellent choice for people new to the Apple Watch ecosystem.

Industry observers note that the Apple Watch Series 12, however, is the best Apple Watch for most people. There are major improvements to the health tracking capabilities, offering meaningful steps forward in what the Apple Watch can tell you about yourself. In the two months I’ve had mine, I’ve come to appreciate the more frequent heart rate measurement and readiness score.

  • Industry observers note that whether you're looking for a PlayStation 5 Digital Edition, a PS5 with a disc drive, or the flagship PlayStation 5 Pro, you won't find them at major online retailers.
  • You still have some options for obtaining a PS5, but none of them are great.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there may be a ton of Black Friday deals on electronics, toys, and gadgets out there, but don't get your hopes up if you're looking for a PlayStation 5. Not only are they not discounted, but the combination of international chip shortages, high demand caused by the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, and the general holiday shopping frenzy has also made it nearly impossible to purchase a new, unbundled PlayStation 5 at any price—nearly impossible, but not impossible.

Industry observers note that whether you're looking for a PlayStation 5 Digital Edition, a PS5 with a disc drive, or the flagship PlayStation 5 Pro, you won't find them at major online retailers. PlayStation Direct lists all three consoles as "presently unavailable." Best Buy suggests making an account with them to "improve your odds" of getting one. I can't find a listing for a new PS5 on Amazon either.

You still have some options for obtaining a PS5, but none of them are great. Many refurbished PS5s are selling for well above the list price of a newly introduced unit. There are some bundled, special editions available, but you'll likely be paying a ton for those. If you're willing to get your hands dirty by dealing with the wild west of Facebook Marketplace, you might be able to track down a used PlayStation 5 at a reasonable price, but approach with extreme caution.

If you're looking for a refurbished PlayStation 5, the best way to avoid a headache is to focus on who did the refurbishing. Buying refurbished electronics directly from a manufacturer is generally safer than buying from a third party, and in this case, it's cheaper too. PlayStation Direct is offering a "Certified Refurbished PlayStation 5 Console" for the relatively reasonable price of $519, while a refurbished Slim sells for $499. But if you're in the market, I'd lock it in quick: PlayStation Direct is already out of refurbished PS5 Pros.

Amazon's Renewed program has some strict requirements for third parties to stay in the program, like keeping defect rates under 0.8%, but refurbished PlayStation 5s are going for a premium on Amazon at the moment. A quick look at the site reveals that the price of a refurbished PlayStation 5 is hovering near $900; a refurbished PS5 Slim will run you somewhere around $750, and the current average price of a refurbished PS5 Pro has ballooned to over $1,700. These are well above the retail prices of $649 for the standard version, $599 for the digital version, and $899 for the flagship Pro version of the PlayStation 5.

There are some bundled versions of the console listed for sale online too. If you buy one of these, you're getting a upcoming console and some other piece of hardware or a game, but there's a ton of upcharge at the moment. They're generally more expensive than the original price and more expensive than refurbished units as well. Here are some examples:.

Best Buy lists this PS5 Pro with PlayStation Portal Remote for $2,134.99.

GameStop lists a Ghost of Yotei Gold Limited Edition PS5 bundle for $769.99 ($731.49 for GameStop Pros).

Best Buy lists a PS5 Slim with an external drive for $979.99.

By far the largest used market for anything in the U.S. is Facebook Marketplace, including PlayStation 5s. I checked out my local Marketplace, and there are a lot of listings for the console within a 40-mile radius of Los Angeles. The average price of used PS5 consoles here is hovering between $300 and $500, which seems fairly reasonable. But with Facebook Marketplace, the number of potential red flags rises with the demand for the product.

Sources indicate that I've bought and sold a fair number of things on Marketplace with no problems beyond the occasional flaky person, and I've written a list of hacks for the service, but I wasn't covering a "shortage buying" situation like this. Scams tend to rise with demand, so when I see a listing for a $150 PS5 console (that contains the text "$250 or best offer"), I'm suspicious. It could have been posted by someone who doesn't know what they have, but I wouldn't count on it. If you're buying a PS5 on Marketplace, check the model and generation details very carefully against the actual item. Make sure the seller is offering what you want and not a PlayStation 4 with PS5 games. Verify how it was stored and the condition it's in. But it ultimately can come down to vibes: Don't let your desire to score a PlayStation 5 get in the way of your gut check about the seller or situation.

In a recent development, in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

There is an abundance of media based on Game of Thrones, the TV show, as opposed to the original source material. For the vast majority of people, it is the faces of Kit Harington, Peter Dinklage, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, and Lena Headey that they remember. So, in the many Game of Thrones video games, for example, their faces are the ones modeled, rather than whole new interpretations of the characters.

Industry observers note that however, while the abundance of upcoming Game of Thrones spin-offs and adaptations may more closely resemble the show, a brand-fresh release goes back to those original novels to offer a unique experience that fans of the books will enjoy. It is absolutely aimed at dedicated fans who love all things A Song of Ice and Fire, as well as tabletop enthusiasts looking for a new wargaming experience they can truly sink their teeth into.

It has been revealed that there have been Game of Thrones board games in the past, but, as aforementioned, these have more often than not adapted the show and not the books. Well, A Song of Ice and Fire: Tactics aims to rectify that with a brand-upcoming tabletop skirmish game that offers a completely fresh take on the many factions and characters featured within the original novels. This new tabletop game is developed by CMON, a studio that has worked with a number of major IPs to great success in the past, including Marvel, DC, and Dune.

A Song of Ice and Fire: Tactics, like the many skirmish tabletop games before it (Halo: Flashpoint is a good comparison), is a wargame for two players that sees each one control a small force of miniatures in a turn-based battle. Utilizing action points, abilities, different unit types, dice, and more, players will attempt to overwhelm the other player and kill their way to victory. It is a combat-focused experience that veers away from the diplomatic politicking of the books and more into the bloody battles.

There are a number of products within the A Song of Ice and Fire: Tactics game that are set to be made available to the public through retail. The best place to start is the A Song of Ice and Fire: Tactics: Battle of the Trident Starter Set, which gives you two warbands, dice, stat sheets, rulebooks, and everything else you need to get started. There are also expansions with other warbands based on iconic factions such as the Brotherhood Without Banners, as well as major sets.

It has been revealed that A Song of Ice and Fire: Tactics was crowdfunded successfully all the way back in February 2024 via Gamefound, but it has yet to be distributed to backers. It is still in production, although a release date has yet to be confirmed by the studio. CMON has posted a few upcoming updates via the Gamefound page and will undoubtedly post the official release date there as well. It is likely that it'll finally be released in 2027, at which point A Song of Ice and Fire (as well as Game of Thrones) fans can finally get their hands on it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it’s not every day you see a movie where talking sheep get to be the stars. But Kyle Balda’s “The Sheep Detectives” does exactly that. The Amazon MGM film flips the whodunnit formula on its head with a barnyard murder mystery in which a group of sheep have to solve the murder of their beloved shepherd. Much of the film’s success can be attributed to the juxtaposition between a whimsical plot and the realism with which it’s executed. The sheep might talk and solve crimes, but they look like real animals you’d find on any farm.

Industry observers note that during the VFX section of IndieWire’s recent Craft Roundtables, “The Sheep Detectives” Visual Effects Supervisor Graham Page broke down the meticulous research process that made the sheep look so lifelike. Related Stories How Disney’s ‘Hexed’ Reinvents the Witch Through Animation How Much of Quentin Tarantino’s Scrapped Film ‘The Movie Critic’ Made It Into ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’?

It has been revealed that “To make them look real, talking about practical and how important that is, I from Day One felt like you had to base these characters on real sheep,” Page stated. “We filmed [real sheep] with multiple cameras and getting on boxes. We had a script, almost, like ‘These are the things the sheep need to do in the film.’ Even before an animator can touch it, another artist modeled the skeleton and the muscle and fat. And then you have a rigger and a facial artist, all of these artists.”.

He went on to explain how that research process produced character-defining details that they would not have discovered any other way.

In a recent development, “We started to come up with what we would call ‘Sheep-isms’ that help kind of bring some of that natural movement,” he said. “There’s a little ear twitch. And a human can’t twitch their ear, but it felt so right. We were like ‘This is really nice,’ and it emphasized the character and the story and the emotion. But it was brought out of a sheep.”.

The director of Focker-in-Law has addressed the comedy's ending and whether it teases another sequel for the long-standing franchise.

The latest sequel to the 2000 movie Meet the Parents introduces Skyler Gisondo as Greg and Pam's son and Ariana Grande as his girlfriend, Olivia Jones. After the Focker and Byrnes family's shenanigans cause chaos, the couple gets engaged, and Olivia seemingly teases a Focker-in-Law sequel. The movie's ending memorably features Olivia declaring that Greg and Pam need to meet her parents. Now, the director of the 2026 comedy has addressed whether that line was truly part of a major strategy or just a throwaway gag.

It has been revealed that on November 25, Variety published a transcript of its interview with Focker-in-Law's director and co-writer, John Hamburg. During that discussion, the creative mind behind the comedy was asked whether the film was designed to set up a forthcoming sequel. In response, he remarked another Fockers movie could happen if it feels "organic" and even revealed he has ideas about who could play Olivia's parents if it does. Check out Hamburg's comments below:.

It has been revealed that variety: The movie ends with a teaser. Do you proposal to make another "Focker" movie?

John Hamburg: Look, I have no one to blame but myself. I wrote that line. Maybe there’s more to mine, but only if it’s organic and feels like there’s a reason for it to exist. Talk to me after Thanksgiving weekend.

Variety: Do you have actors in mind to play the parents of Ariana’s character?

John Hamburg: I have some people in mind, but there’s no way I could talk about this right now.

In a recent development, based on early indications, there are a lot of reasons to think that producing another movie in the highly successful film series could make sense for everyone involved. For example, even though Focker-in-Law's reviews are underwhelming, it right now holds an impressive 87% Popcornmeter score on Rotten Tomatoes based on more than 250 user ratings.

That said, any potential intends to make a sequel to Focker-in-Law could fall apart if the movie fails at the box office, and it has a massive stumbling block to overcome in that regard. According to The Hollywood Reporter, it was produced on an estimated $90 million budget. Given the all-star cast that would be involved in any sequel, especially if stars were cast as Olivia's parents, a fifth film would also almost certainly cost a hefty sum to make.

According to recent reports, while it is still unclear if there will be another movie in the Fockers film franchise, viewers who want to see more will no doubt be happy to know that the co-writer and director of Focker-in-Law seems open to the prospect. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Critical Role is by far the most popular Dungeons & Dragons actual-play show, with more than a decade of role-playing antics including one-shots, live indicates, and hundreds of hours of tabletop campaigns. Its adventures are so beloved that the manufacturer has even adapted them into the Prime video animated series The Legend of Vox Machina and The Mighty Nein.

Industry observers note that despite that popularity, one thing still makes it hard to get into the show: the length of its episodes. Critical Role episodes typically run three to four hours, but during the Convergence arc of its latest campaign, episodes stretched to around five hours. Episode 31, "Trick of the Light," ran for a staggering 6 hours and 18 minutes.

After that peak, Critical Role episodes settled back into a range of 3 to 4 hours. In the latest episode of the Fireside Chat ask-me-anything series, Critical Role co-founder and creative director Marisha Ray explained that shorter episodes are here to stay.

Asked via Critical Role’s Discord server about why episodes have recently gotten shorter, Ray responded,.

According to recent reports, episodes of Critical Role’s Campaign 4 typically air on Thursdays at 7 p.m. Pacific Time, which is 10 p.m. Eastern Time and 3 a.m. for folks like me in the U.K. Staying up for three or four hours is a huge commitment, and even devoted Critters might need to go to bed before finishing.

Ray explained that Critical Role’s cast and crew also wanted shorter episodes.

Industry observers note that “There are several reasons: there are laws, our crew wants to go home, we want to make sure that they’re not starving by the end of the night, they want to go home and see their children,” Ray remarked. “With production, if you go past certain times and you go into what are called meal penalties, or you start going into overtime, and don’t get me wrong, we're super happy to pay it all, and pay it all the time here in Critical Role. But also, we don’t want to be toxic about that. We want to be mindful of that.”.

It has been revealed that ray said the cast and crew typically shoot Critical Role episodes at night, often after a long day of voice acting or administrative work. The cast also stays behind for 10- to 20-minute Cooldown episodes. That's a lot of work.

We can all relate to the cast’s despair when an episode ends, and we’re left wanting more. But what matters more is giving the cast and crew of Critical Role the time and space they need to rest instead of pushing themselves to exhaustion.

‘All of a Sudden’: Why Does an 11-Minute Scene Centered on a Whiteboard Lecture Work So Well Onscreen?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (959 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it is an unorthodox sequence.
  • While a guest on this week’s Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast, Hamaguchi acknowledged the whiteboard is not what we generally consider to be cinematic, but then again neither is the three-hour-and-17-minute film about two women who form a powerful bond by talking about life, their life’s work, and the ever so sexy topic of eldercare for dementia patients.
  • And yet “All of a Sudden” blew away the world’s toughest critics at Cannes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it is an unorthodox sequence. In the middle of “All of a Sudden,” Mari (Tao Okamoto) pulls out a whiteboard and markers to diagram the principles of nature vs. capitalism for her upcoming friend Marie-Lou (Virginie Efira). The scene lasts 11 minutes and digs into material you would expect in a university seminar, not the latest cinematic achievement from the Oscar-winning director of “Drive My Car,” Ryūsuke Hamaguchi.

While a guest on this week’s Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast, Hamaguchi acknowledged the whiteboard is not what we generally consider to be cinematic, but then again neither is the three-hour-and-17-minute film about two women who form a powerful bond by talking about life, their life’s work, and the ever so sexy topic of eldercare for dementia patients. Related Stories How Disney’s ‘Hexed’ Reinvents the Witch Through Animation How Much of Quentin Tarantino’s Scrapped Film ‘The Movie Critic’ Made It Into ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’?

And yet “All of a Sudden” blew away the world’s toughest critics at Cannes. Now, its distributor, Neon, heads into this weekend’s holiday theatrical release believing it has a legit shot at winning over the more commercially oriented Oscar voters — and becoming one of the (increasingly common) foreign-language Best Picture nominations. Neon similarly released “Sentimental Value” and “The Secret Agent” to Best Picture nominations the year before.

The whiteboard scene is not an extraneous aside, but a critical turning point in the women’s relationship. We asked the film’s writer/director why it not only works, but was deemed vital to the film.

“In trying to answer why this somehow works, I think there’s a few layers to it,” said Hamaguchi while on IndieWire’s Filmmaker Toolkit podcast. “And one maybe is because it really is something that is far removed from what is generally considered as cinematic. Perhaps because of that, it brings about a certain suspense, where you wonder, ‘OK, what is this for? What is this actually going to do?’ And there’s a certain sense of wondering that happens.”.

The scene comes a little over an hour into the film. Neither woman wants their magical evening to end. Mari follows Marie-Lou to her job as director of a nursing home, where she struggles to implement her passion project, “Huminitude,” a patient-centered care method based on touch and eye contact, which Mari sees in action. What prompts Mari’s whiteboard seminar is an attempt to help her new companion put into perspective the resistance she faces in implementing Huminitude and open the door to problem-solving.

“I think the second part [of why the scene works] really comes down to the efforts of the actors that are performing this scene,” remarked Hamaguchi of Okamoto and Efira, who shared the Best Actress Prize at Cannes. “For Tao, I think it was an incredibly difficult scene to perform because first of all she really needed to understand all of the concepts that she was describing here and to really understand everything intellectually. And so in her preparation she did read a lot of the relevant books to really understand what she is talking about.”.

Hamaguchi believes the key to his dialogue-driven film is not necessarily how the words are spoken, but the performance of the listening and how the words are received. In Efira’s whiteboard scene, we see a shift from determined frustration to open enthusiasm that changes the direction of the film itself.

“The attitude of listening that Virginie portrays in this moment, I think, is very important and really supports this scene,” said Hamaguchi. “She’s not uninterested in what is going on, but in fact she feels that this is something that she should really be exploring together and she’s there and very much present. And I think this attitude of interest and curiosity really starts to work on the audience as well. And so in that sense I think ultimately this scene really works because of the actors’ performances.”.

One topic that comes up in most post-screening Q&As is that both actresses were not working in the native language. Hamaguchi himself had to work with an interpreter to direct his leads. This is not the first time Hamaguchi has worked this way. On the podcast, he said that, in his experience directing the play inside “Drive My Car,” the language barrier was less of a hindrance and could even aid actors in listening to one another, as shown in the whiteboard scene.

Sources indicate that “I felt that, in fact, this kind of difficulty that exists can in fact provide an environment for even more heightened concentration than you might have if you were speaking the same language,” said Hamaguchi. “ I think that actually when you can actually hear a lot and get a lot of information from somebody’s voice, you can, in fact, precisely feel just how concentrated the person is when they’re saying something by listening to their voice.”.

Asked if any of his collaborators or producers ever questioned the whiteboard scene after reading the script, Hamaguchi said no, and speculated why: “Because it’s so unusual, I think people understood that this is something that I really wanted to do.”.

“There were some questions around, ‘This section feels a little long. Is there anything we can do about that?’” recalled Hamaguchi, adding that he made a concerted effort to cut his four-hour script to a three-hour, 16-minute running time.

“For me, I was ultimately trying to bring in the shortest version that I felt was accurate for this moment. But ultimately, there is this understanding that this moment is a very notable turning point within the film, and so I believe that the producers also understood this.”.

“All of a Sudden” is now playing in select theaters.
